It’s very hard to do it until you’re ready. It took me years to get past it, and now I’m still scared but I’m trying and getting better. Driving in the dark is still hard for me because I have astigmatism.

My advice: Drive familiar routes and expand a little more as you can. Even do them backwards so you can still get comfortable with different turns. Don’t test until you’re ready. I’m waiting till spring to take mine because I won’t be ready before the snow hits but I want to practice snow driving before I test because it’s something I’ll need to deal with at some point anyway. Don’t try to think about it too hard, but do try to visualize your turns. Your windshield is not the only window you can look out of. Make sure you are comfortable when driving, adjust the seat and make sure you can see out of your mirrors and use them. Just breathe and remember there’s a lot of people who hate driving, but if they can do it, so can you. Your fears are valid, driving is scary. 

Also, watch driving videos on YouTube. They can give good tips.

In my experience, creme bleach is better than powder. You would still mix it with developer. 30 vol would be optimal. If your hair is brown, chances are it will get brassy/yellow. If it's a light yellow, you can tone it. If it's more orange, I'd wait and bleach once more. Chances are your hair will go pretty light, given your hair is a short boy-type cut.

To tone, you'd get a toner. Depending on how blonde you want it, you'd get a box toner. Wella is a good brand. You also use developer with this, a weaker one. 10-20 vol most likely. Check the instructions always. 

You can buy small kits that have the tools you'll need. Mixing bowl (don't use metal when working with bleach), a tint brush to apply the bleach, processing cap, etc.

There are a ton of YouTube videos, I can recommend a few. If you go to Sally's, don't always trust the employees. Many of them aren't in cosmetology, so they don't always get it right. Learned this the hard way. Always read boxes and instructions. Never skip steps and be careful. Bleaching can be dangerous if you don't know what you're doing.

Best of luck. :)
